newsitem.title: USA: Suspects caught, charged in triple murder.
newsitem.headline: Suspects caught, charged in triple murder.

text.p: Six people were arrested in Arizona Tuesday and charged with killing a Tennessee couple and one of their two children, who were left sprawled in the arms of their dead parents on a rural road, police said Tuesday.

Greene County Sheriff Terry Jones said three females and three males ranging in age from 14 to 20 were in custody at Douglas, Arizona, charged with "felony murder in the commission of a theft." They were apprehended in a van stolen from the victims, he said.
"We really don't know what caused them to do this," Jones told Reuters. "We are treating it as a robbery-homicide." Those charged are all from Kentucky, he said.
The bodies of Vidar Lillelid, 34, and his wife Delphia, 28, of Knoxville, Tenn., were found Sunday along a gravel road in hilly northeast Tennessee.
"When officers arrived the little boy was on his mother's chest and the little girl on the left side of the other parent's chest," he said.

The girl, Tabitha, 6, died in a hospital Monday. The other child, Peter, 3, was in serious condition at a hospital. Both children had been shot in the head and the family's belongings were missing along with their van.
